title: Internship in Film/Television
description: An opportunity for training, career sampling, and contacts in the film or television industry. Required are approximately 100 hours of work per quarter, a final five-page report, and a supervisor's letter of verification.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies majors only.

title: Advanced Film Analysis
description: A study of the basic formal dimensions of cinema: narration, space, time, and sound.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46 and 70 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Independent Studies.
description: Selected research under the direction of a faculty member.
prerequisites_raw: Consent of instructor and department.

title: History of Cinema: The Silent Film
description: International film history from the camera obscura to the close of the silent era in the late 1920's. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology are considered.
prerequisites_raw: FAMST 96 with a minimum grade of C.

title: History of Cinema: The Silent Film - Honors
description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated Letters and Science Honors Students.
prerequisites_raw: Student must be concurrently enrolled in Film and Media Studies 101A

title: History of Cinema: The Development of Sound Film
description: International film history from the advent of talkies through the late 1950s. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology is considered.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.

title: History of Cinema: The Development of Sound - Honors
description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated Letters and Science Honors Students.
prerequisites_raw: Student must be concurrently enrolled in Film and Media Studies 101B

title: History of Cinema: New Waves and Beyond
description: International film history since 1959. Historical accounts of film as an aesthetic form, a social force, an economic institution, and a technology is considered.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.

title: History of Cinema: New Waves and Beyond
description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated Letters and Science Honors Students.
prerequisites_raw: Student must be concurrently enrolled in Film and Media Studies 101C

title: History of Electronic Media: Telegraphy to Early Television
description: International history of electronic media and broadcasting from telegraphy to early television. Historical accounts of telegraphy, radio, and early television as cultural forms, communications technologies, and social political and economic institutions are considered.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.

title: History of Electronic Media: Network TV to the Digital Era
description: International history of electronic media from the 1960s through the present day. Historical accounts of broadcasting, cable, satellites and digital media as cultural forms, communications technologies and social, political and economic institutions are considered.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 96 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Film History: International Cinema from 1989-Present
description: International film history since 1989. Focuses on the expansion of independent and corporate-backed filmmaking around the world after the end of the Cold War as well as on a wide range of industrial, technological, cultural, and aesthetic changes.
prerequisites_raw: FAMST 96 with a grade of C or better.

title: Film History: International Cinema from 1989-Present - Honors
description: Students receive one unit for the honors seminar. Intended for highly motivated FAMST majors.
prerequisites_raw: Student must be concurrently enrolled in Film and Media Studies 101F

title: Acting and Directing Workshop
description: Designed as an introduction to the fundamentals and interaction of acting and directing in the creative process of producing a film or video. Every student will write, perform in, direct, and record on video a short work.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46; and consent of instructor; upper-division film and majors only

title: Project Development
description: A workshop approach to the development of a short film project. Course covers writing, budget preparation, and preproduction, with particular attention to final distribution needs.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46; and, Film and Media Studies 104, or 106A-B; and consent of instructor.

title: Introduction to Production Technology
description: An introduction to video production and technology, focusing on the fundamental concepts of the moving image including core aspects of shooting, lighting, sound-recording & editing. Lectures complement the hands-on labs by covering key concepts, dissecting various productions, and learning the workflow from pre to post-production.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46; open to film and media majors only.

title: Historic Production
description: Teaches film history as a production workshop. Students will be introduced to the primary technologies and working methods used during three distinct eras in the development of the motion picture. The class will write and produce scenes on 16mm film reflecting the styles and techniques of the silent era.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46; open to film studies majors only.

title: Crew Production Part One
description: Instruction in the basic techniques of filmmaking via the production of crew projects over two consecutive quarters. Pre-production through principal photography.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, 102 or 104 or 107; and consent of instructor.

title: Crew Production part two
description: Instruction in the basic techniques of filmmaking via the production of crew projects over two consecutive quarters. Post-production through exhibition.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, 102 or 104 or 107; and consent of instructor.

title: Introduction to Animation
description: A look at the techniques and history of animation with emphasis on the major styles and methods of production, including cel, direct, photo, three-dimensional and computer. Close examination of significant films combined with production of a class project.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46 or upper-division standing.

title: Contemporary Animation
description: Covers the basics of both classical and computer animation from a practical and theoretical point of view. Field trips are taken.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 107.

title: Short Project Production
description: A workshop approach to the production of individual, short projects. Each student produces a project by the end of the quarter. Admission to this course is determined by creative portfolio.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46 or consent of instructor.

title: Special Topics in Film Production
description: Focus on one or more aspects of film production such as music, writing, directing, design, acting, independent filmmaking, cinematography, producing. Topics will vary.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.

title: Special Topics in Film Production: Impact Media
description: Compelling story telling drives social and environmental change. The aim of this course is to develop the skills of a multi-platform producer. Students learn how to create professional media and impact strategies that influence behavior and drive innovation on contemporary media platforms from instagram to the big screen.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46; and, consent of instructor.
